div.head: Rect 1
div.ab: [1] Ðegenes lagu. Ðegenlagu is, þæt he sy his bocrihtes wyrðe ⁊ þæt he ðreo ðinc of his lande do: fyrdfæreld ⁊ burhbote ⁊ brycgeweorc.
De lege taini. Taini lex est, ut sit dignus rectitudine testamenti sui et ut tria faciat pro terra sua, scilicet expeditionem, burhbotam et brugbotam.
ĐEGENES LAGV . ĐEGEN LAGV IS þæt he sy his boc rihtes wyr|ðe . 7 þæt he ðreo ðinc of his lande do fyrd|færeld . 7 burhbote 7 brycgeweorc .
Ðegenes lagu Ðegenlagu is þæt he sy his bocrihtes wyrðe, and þæt he ðreo ðinc of his lande do: fyrdfæreld and burhbote and brycgeweorc.

Recht und Pflicht des Thegn. Thegnrecht und -pflicht ist, dass er seines Urkundenrechtes geniesse und von seinem Lande drei Dinge [dem Staate] leiste: Landwehr-Heerfahrt und Festungsherstellung und Brückenwerk [Strassenbau].

The right and duty of the thegn [as lord of a great estate]. The thegn's law is that he be entitled to his charter-right [i.e. the privilege the king granted him by the charter by which he confirmed or granted him the estate] and that he render three things [to the state] from his land: service in the army, repair of fortifications, and bridge-work [road-building].

The law of the thegn The law of the thegn is that he should be worthy of his book-rights, and that from his land he [must] do three things: levy a company, and be liable for the building and repair of town walls, and build bridges.

The Duty of the Thane The thane’s duty is to fulfill the obligations of his charter, and do three things with his estate: raise a militia, oversee the upkeep of the buildings and walls, and repair the bridges.

div.note: There should be an English translation by Thom Gobbitt to go with his text in column T (Early English Laws); it has not been found yet (the site was not working in October 2026), so the translation in column U has not been checked against it; Liebermann's text is from B (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 383, p. 96, after Dunsæte, c. 1125, then belonging to St Paul's, London), the same manuscript as the modern edition. The headings are in red; some show Middle English forms (16 f.) and, where the Quadripartitus lacks them, are perhaps not archetypal and probably none are original. The Quadripartitus has a heading ‘De dignitate hominum (Rectitudines singularum personarum)’; Liebermann's German heading is ‘Gerechtsame der Leute [des Edelguts]’. Liebermann thinks the author a clerically trained reeve of a thegn's estate chartered by the king, writing late West Saxon, after 960 and before 1066, perhaps after 1017; Gerefa appears as its continuation. Das Possessiv bedeutet hier den, der den Vorteil geniesst.—Dieser Thegn untersteht keinem Magnaten oder Prälaten, da sonst die Pflicht diesem gegenüber vorkäme. Bocland (s. d. Gl 1 D) hat hier die engere Bed.: ‘vom König verbrieft’

The possessive here denotes the one who enjoys the benefit. — This thegn is not subject to any magnate or prelate, since otherwise his duty towards him would be mentioned. Bocland (see that word in Gl 1 D) has here the narrower meaning ‘secured by royal charter’

Nicht etwa Testierfreiheit ist gemeint (gegen Kemble Saxons I 180, wohl aus Q), wenn diese auch freilich in der boc (s. Gl: bocland 6) mitenthalten war. Q meint nur ‘Urkunde’ mit testamentum; s. d. Wb

What is meant is not, say, freedom of testamentary disposition (against Kemble Saxons I 180, probably on the basis of Q), even though this was admittedly also contained in the boc (see Gl: bocland 6). By testamentum Q means only ‘charter’; see that word in Wb
d. h. des Vorrechtes, welches ihm der König verbrieft hat in der Urkunde, kraft welcher er ihm das Gut bestätigte oder verlieh
i.e. of the privilege which the king secured to him in the charter by virtue of which he confirmed or granted him the estate

Ebd. Brücke 1c. 2. Q setzt das im 12. Jh. allein fortlebende Wort ein. Nicht bloss nahe den Gütern des Adels und Kirchenstifts (wie Andrews Manor 125) ward für Brücken gesorgt: auch an städtische und militärische ist zu denken

Ibid. Brücke 1c. 2. Q substitutes the word that alone survived in the 12th cent. Bridges were not provided only near the estates of the nobility and of ecclesiastical foundations (as Andrews Manor 125 holds): urban and military ones must also be considered

Oftmals geben die verschiedenen Rezensionen des Q mehrfache Übersetzungsversuche zu Einem Angelsächs. Texte. Vielleicht lautete dieser hier Be manna gerihtum, was Q De dignitate (später darüber rectitudines) hominum übersetzte. Die Wörter singularum personarum dagegen gehören nur dem Rubrikator letzter Ausgabe selbst, da er sie vor Norðleod I 459¹ ebenfalls als Überschrift setzt

The various recensions of Q often give several attempts at translating a single Anglo-Saxon text. Perhaps the text here read Be manna gerihtum, which Q translated De dignitate (later, written above it, rectitudines) hominum. The words singularum personarum, on the other hand, belong only to the rubricator of the last edition himself, since he likewise sets them as a heading before Norðleod I 459¹
